findings.title: A certificate under a script's stake credential counts as another signer, so partialSign=false is refused and the window says others must sign
findings.scenario: A Mesh-style dApp calls signTx(tx, false) (partialSign false, Mesh's default). Its tx has one input, the account's found UTxO A (5 ₳), change back to 0/0, fee 0.2 ₳, and one certificate: StakeRegistration(ScriptHash S), the old-style registration of a script's reward account. A deployer registering a withdraw-zero validator does this, and the ledger needs no witness at all for it. inspect then takes cred = ScriptHash, so stake_hash() is None, so `hash` is None, the match falls to `None => others_sign += 1`, and complete is false. readTx refuses before the window opens, with dapp.needsOtherKeys (ProofGeneration): "This transaction needs signatures the wallet can't give…". The ledger accepts the transaction with the account's payment witness alone. A Conway Reg, a delegation or a vote delegation of a script credential behaves the same: it needs only its script and redeemer, which the site supplies. With partialSign true it signs, but the window shows "You sign your part only. Others sign too before it's sent.", which is false.
findings.since: fe8b7748 (chunk 15, the first connector; in 1.0.0 and every release since)
findings.evidence: cip30.rs:1068-1073 `fn stake_hash(cred) -> Option<&Hash<28>> { AddrKeyhash(h) => Some(h), ScriptHash(_) => None }`; cip30.rs:1595 `let hash = cred.and_then(stake_hash);` and 1597-1611: `Some(h) if *h == keys.stake => …`, `Some(h) if witnessed => foreign_keys.insert(*h)`, `// A script's stake credential, or a registration that needs no signature.\n Some(_) => {}`, `// Pools, the committee and DReps sign with keys this wallet doesn't hold.\n None => others_sign += 1`. A script credential can never reach `Some(_)`, so the comment's intent is never met. cip30.rs:1841-1842 `others_sign += foreign_keys.len(); let complete = others_sign == 0 && unknown.is_empty();`. cip30.rs:1958-1962 sign_tx bails `!request.partial_sign && !summary.complete`. extension/src/background/dapp.ts readTx: `if (!partialSign && !summary.complete) throw refuse(TxSignError.ProofGeneration, … t("dapp.needsOtherKeys" …))`. By contrast a script withdrawal is counted correctly, at cip30.rs:1656-1657 `StakePayload::Script(_) => false` (no foreign key). wasm/README.md:93 says signDappTx "Refuses without partialSign when anyone else must sign too". The existing test cip30_test.rs:482 a_stake_certificate_says_whose_stake_key_it_names has a script delegation, but with partial_sign true and a foreign key beside it, so complete isn't pinned for it.
findings.fix: Decide by the credential's kind, not by whether a key hash came out. A script credential needs no key, so count nothing, as the withdrawal branch already does. Keep `others_sign += 1` only for the certificates that carry no credential here (pool registration, pool retirement) and for committee certificates whose cold credential is a key. AuthCommitteeHot and ResignCommitteeCold with a script cold credential are the same class. Correct the comment at 1607. Test (wasm/tests, cip30_test.rs helpers): body(vec![input(TX_A,1)], vec![out(&ours(Receive,0),1_800_000,None)]) with certificates [StakeRegistration(StakeCredential::ScriptHash(Hash::new([6;28])))] and partial_sign false. inspect_tx should give others_sign 0 and complete true, and sign_tx should be Ok. Today it is Err("needs signatures the wallet can't give").
findings.known_check: I searched backlog.md and docs/archive/plans for "script's stake credential", "script credential", "stake_hash", "others_sign", "othersSign", "needsOtherKeys", "partialSign" and "complete". There is nothing on it. backlog line 156 covers the account's other key hashes in a stake position, a different shape.

findings.title: A key address whose key hash equals the Seedelf contract's script hash is labelled Seedelf Wallet's contract, so a burn shows as a Seedelf payment
findings.scenario: A site's tx pays 100 ₳ of the account's to an enterprise KEY address (header 0x60 on preprod, 0x61 on mainnet) whose 28-byte key hash is the Seedelf contract's script hash. Nobody holds a key with that hash, so the money is gone for good. If the output carries a payable register datum, the window's Pays row reads "Seedelf Wallet's contract" and its privacy callout says "It pays a Seedelf. Nothing on chain says whose…". Without a datum it warns "It pays Seedelf Wallet's contract without a register: whatever goes there, anyone can take.", when in fact no one can. Transaction details (decode.rs:1370, which checks is_script()) shows the same output as a plain key address, so the two views disagree. The amount leaving is right. The label of who gets it is wrong, and the site gains nothing.
findings.evidence: cip30.rs:1384-1395: `let script = matches!(&address, Address::Shelley(s) if s.payment().is_script()); let seedelf = match &address { Address::Shelley(s) if *s.payment().as_hash() == contract_hash => Some(if inline…is_register_datum {"register"} else {"none"}) …`. pallas-addresses-0.35.1/src/lib.rs:138-141 `pub fn as_hash(&self) -> &Hash<28> { Self::Key(x) => x, Self::Script(x) => x }`, so a key part matches. decode.rs:1370 `let seedelf = s.payment().is_script() && *s.payment().as_hash() == *contract;`. extension/src/ui/dapp.ts:41-56 paidTo puts `p.seedelf` before `p.script`, giving t("dappUi.paid.seedelfContract") = "Seedelf Wallet's contract". DappApprovals.tsx:1185-1194 shows dappUi.warn.noRegister for "none" and dappUi.privacy.paysSeedelfAccount for "register".
findings.fix: Add `s.payment().is_script() &&` to the match guard, as decode.rs does. For the class: the worker's contract matching by Koios `payment_cred` alone (contract-scan.ts:429, sessions.ts:2954, the data layer's credential routes) reads a key credential and a script credential with the same hash alike. Those lanes should check whether a key address with the contract's hash can enter the private balance. Test: out(&Address::Shelley(ShelleyAddress::new(Network::Testnet, ShelleyPaymentPart::Key(contract_hash), ShelleyDelegationPart::Null)), 2_000_000, Some(REGISTER_DATUM)) should give paid[0].seedelf None and script false. Today it gives Some("register").
findings.known_check: I searched backlog.md and archive/plans for "is_script", "as_hash", and "key address" or "key hash" with "contract hash". None found. cip30_test.rs:1375 a_payment_into_seedelf_says_whether_it_has_a_register uses only the real script address.

findings.title: Transaction details converts a big number to decimal in quadratic time, so a site's 60 KB bignum freezes the worker for tens of seconds per open
findings.scenario: A site calls signTx with a transaction of up to 64 KiB (the read limit). It holds one found input of the account's, so the window opens. A redeemer's argument, or a witness datum, is a tag-2 big number whose byte string is about 65,000 bytes, starting 0x01 so the nesting walk reads one item and moves on. Pallas reads any length, and inspect never converts big numbers, so the prompt shows normally. When the user presses Transaction details, tx-view.ts:184 runs decodeTx in the worker: plutus_tree → big_int_text → decimal(). That makes about 2.4·L ≈ 157,000 digits, each a full pass over all ~65,000 bytes with a carried division, about 1.0×10^10 dependent steps plus a leading-zero scan of about 5×10^9. By that count it is tens of seconds natively and more in WebAssembly. For that long the worker's single WebAssembly instance and event loop answer nothing: the wallet's pages, other sites and the alarms all wait. Every press repeats it. The ledger's own Plutus data decoder bounds a big number to 64 bytes, so this transaction could never land, but the window doesn't need it to.
findings.since: b67ea43c (chunk 17's datum tree, after 1.0.0; in 1.1.0 onward)
findings.evidence: decode.rs:470-476 big_int_text calls `decimal(bytes.as_slice(), …)` for BigUInt/BigNInt. decode.rs:480-512: `while n.iter().any(|b| *b != 0) { let mut rest = 0u16; for byte in n.iter_mut() { let now = rest * 256 + u16::from(*byte); *byte = (now / 10) as u8; rest = now % 10; } digits.push(…) }`. The inner loop always runs over the whole vector, leading zeros included, so the cost is digits×L. pallas-primitives-0.35.1/src/plutus_data.rs:446-453: BoundedBytes::decode concatenates every chunk with no length bound, and :236 decodes tag 2 into BigUInt with it. cip30.rs:1145 and decode.rs:620 cap the request at 2×64 KiB of hex. decode.rs:1447/1473 plutus_of(data) decodes each redeemer argument, and :729 plutus_tree each witness datum. extension/src/background/tx-view.ts:184 `JSON.parse(wasm.decodeTx(net, cbor))` runs in the worker. TxDetail.tsx:76-92 decodes when the button is pressed. Not timed (finders run nothing): the figure is an operation count.
findings.fix: Convert word by word: divide by 10^19 over u64 limbs (or 10^9 over u32), emitting 19 digits a pass. That is about 8× fewer inner steps a pass and 19× fewer passes, so ~150× less work, and the same digits. Alternatively, show a number past 64 bytes (more than the ledger takes in Plutus data) as its hex and size, though that touches the owner's "nothing assumed" view. Test (wasm/tests/decode_test.rs): a transaction whose redeemer argument is `c2 59 fde8` + 65,000 bytes, with decode_tx under a time bound and the decimal checked against a reference for a small case.
findings.known_check: I searched backlog.md and archive/plans for "bignum", "big number", "tag 2", "decimal" and "quadratic". chunk-17-transaction-view.md:295-306 records reading big numbers exactly, and MAX_DATUM_NODES records the drawing cost, not the conversion. The backlog's cip30-rust#5 is inspect's datum scan, a different path.

findings.title: getUtxos drops a UTxO's reference script, so a site spending it underpays the Conway fee and the node refuses the signed transaction
findings.scenario: The account's address 0/0 holds a UTxO carrying a reference script. It can be a stranger's (anyone can send one; a 500-byte native script costs them about 3.7 ₳, which becomes the user's) or the user's own, a script deployed to their address through some dApp (about 45 ₳ for 10 KB, so largestFirst lists it first). getUtxos offers it: available() filters only locks and the collateral. utxo_cbor writes it without its script, because KoiosRow has no reference_script field and the function's doc says it isn't passed on. A site builds a transaction spending it and prices the fee from the UTxO it was handed. Conway charges min_fee_ref_script_cost_per_byte (15 lovelace a byte, tiered) for reference scripts on spent inputs too; launch review #12 recorded exactly this refusal for the wallet's own builders, which now price it. So the site's fee is short by about 15 × script size (7,500 lovelace for 500 bytes, 150,000 for 10 KB), and after the user signs, the node refuses with FeeTooSmallUTxO. Every site transaction that picks that UTxO fails until the user locks it in coin control. No money moves.
findings.evidence: cip30.rs:46-59 `pub struct KoiosRow { tx_hash, tx_index, address, value, datum_hash, inline_datum, asset_list }` has no reference script, and serde ignores the field. cip30.rs:284-286 doc: "A reference script on one of the account's own UTxOs isn't passed on." cip30.rs:312-336 writes the map form with keys 0, 1, 2 only, or the legacy array. wasm/src/lib.rs:6809-6815 cip30Utxos calls utxo_cbor on each row. extension/src/background/dapp.ts:1671-1687 available() returns spendable + inflight. coin-control.ts:246-256 account() filters only the collateral and locked outpoints. koios.ts:36-41 and 67-83: the rows carry reference_script, and `trimmed` keeps its `type` and `bytes`. launch-review.md:232 (#12): "Public side: the fee leaves out Conway's reference-script fee for spent inputs, so the node refuses with FeeTooSmallUTxO."
findings.fix: Either read reference_script { type, bytes } into KoiosRow and write it as the output's key 3, `#6.24(bytes .cbor [kind, script])`, forcing the map form so the site sees the output as it is on chain; or leave reference-script UTxOs out of getUtxos and getBalance, as the private side does (balances.ts:475). Test: utxo_cbor of a row with a reference_script should give an output with key 3 that decodes back to that script.
findings.owner_why: Either fix changes what a site is handed: more of the account's UTxO (its script), or fewer UTxOs offered.
findings.known_check: I searched backlog.md and archive/plans for "reference script", "reference_script", and "getUtxos" with "script" or "fee". launch review #12 fixed the wallet's own spends (priced via `measurable`). Nothing covers the connector's getUtxos encoding.

findings.title: getBalance fails for every site once a stranger's token total across the account's UTxOs passes a u64
findings.scenario: A stranger mints their own token three times, 2^63−1 each (the most one mint can hold), into three outputs to the account's 0/0. That costs about 4 ₳, most of which becomes the user's. The worker's getBalance sums every available UTxO's tokens in BigInt (≈2.77×10^19) and passes the total as text to cip30Value. value_cbor parses each quantity as a u64 and throws "a token quantity isn't a whole number: \"27670116110564327421\"". From then on every connected site's getBalance errors; many dApps call it on connect. getUtxos still works. It lasts until the user finds and locks those UTxOs. CIP-30's Value can't hold a quantity past a u64 at all, so some choice has to be made.
findings.evidence: extension/src/background/dapp.ts:1689-1705 balance(): `tokens.set(key, (tokens.get(key) ?? 0n) + BigInt(a.quantity))` … `return this.deps.wasm.cip30Value(lovelace.toString(), JSON.stringify(list))`. wasm/src/lib.rs:6818-6821 calls cip30::value_cbor. cip30.rs:347-356: `let quantity = t.quantity.parse().map_err(|_| anyhow!("a token quantity isn't a whole number: {:?}", t.quantity))?; amount.add_token(…)?` parses as u64 and refuses past one.
findings.fix: Don't fail the whole call for one asset no CIP-30 Value can express. Cap that token at u64::MAX (CIP-30's own ceiling), or leave it out, and keep the error for a malformed quantity. Test: cip30::value_cbor("2000000", &[Token{policy_id, asset_name, quantity: "18446744073709551616"}]) is Err today.
findings.owner_why: Capping or leaving out a token changes what a site is told about the balance (a figure that isn't the sum).
findings.known_check: I searched backlog.md and archive/plans for getBalance with "u64", "overflow", "2^64" and "whole number". None found. backlog cip30-rust#9 (contract token totals saturate) is the sign window's contract_held, a different sum with a different symptom.

findings.title: Byron addresses: a found Byron input fails the whole read, and a Byron payee shows as raw hex
findings.scenario: (a) A site's partial-sign transaction spends a counterparty's UTxO at a Byron address, for example a P2P trade. Koios lists Byron addresses in base58, as db-sync stores them. resolve() finds the row through utxo_info, and inspect's owner() parses it with Address::from_bech32, which reads bech32 only. So the whole read fails with "UTxO …#… has an unreadable address" and the site's transaction is refused, though the ledger accepts it with the counterparty's bootstrap witness. The branch at 1221-1225, meant to count a Byron input as someone else's, can never run. (b) A site's payment to a Byron address shows in Pays as its raw hex ("82d81858…"), because Address::to_bech32 is Err(InvalidForByron) for Byron. The user can't match it to the base58 address they were given. decode.rs:1395-1396 says Pallas writes base58 there, but Transaction details shows the same hex.
findings.evidence: cip30.rs:1191 `let address = Address::from_bech32(&row.address).map_err(|e| anyhow!("UTxO {}#{} has an unreadable address: {e}", …))?;`. cip30.rs:1221-1225 `// A Byron address needs a bootstrap witness this wallet never makes. _ => { foreign_keys.insert(Hash::new([0; 28])); None }`. cip30.rs:1369 `let bech32 = address.to_bech32().unwrap_or_else(|_| address.to_hex());`. pallas-addresses-0.35.1/src/lib.rs:608-612 `Address::Byron(_) => Err(Error::InvalidForByron)`; :617-619 from_bech32 = bech32_to_address, bech32 only; :693-699 Display writes base58 for Byron; :706-720 FromStr tries bech32, then base58, then hex. decode.rs:1395-1397 `// A Byron address has no bech32 form; Pallas writes its base58 for \`to_bech32\`… bech32: address.to_bech32().unwrap_or_else(|_| address.to_hex())`. No test feeds a Byron row: cip30_test.rs:1298 covers Byron outputs' network only, and decode_test.rs has no Byron case.
findings.fix: Read row text with Address::from_str (`row.address.parse::<Address>()`) in owner(), at_script and utxo_cbor. A Byron row must stay never the account's and be network-checked with network_of. Show addresses with Display (`address.to_string()`: base58 for Byron, bech32 otherwise) in Paid, Withdrawal, Proposal, DataFor::shown and decode.rs's DetailAddress.bech32, and correct decode.rs's comment. Test: a found row with a base58 Byron address among the inputs should give others_sign 1 instead of Err; a Byron output's paid[0].address should be its base58.
findings.known_check: I searched backlog.md and archive/plans for "byron". Only chunk-17's witness count and chunk-09 mention it. Commit 28bd1d5e (final review network-dapp-1) handled Byron outputs' network, not Byron rows or how a Byron address is shown.

guards.stops: A site's transaction over 64 KiB (hex over 128 KiB) is refused before any decode (bounds point checks, datum scans and the view).
check_nesting: CBOR nested past 128 levels, the bytes a tag wraps included, is refused before Pallas recurses, which would overflow WebAssembly's stack and kill the instance.
guards.test: cip30_test.rs deeply_nested_data_is_refused_before_it_is_decoded, nesting_inside_a_datums_bytes_counts_too, a_big_numbers_bytes_are_bytes_and_the_check_goes_on_after_them (native only; no WebAssembly test at the 128 boundary)

guards.stops: A body network_id of the other network is refused.
An input or collateral row at a Shelley address on the other network is refused, so a key witness can't spend the account's UTxO there.
owner(): a found input or collateral is the account's by payment, stake or (with governance) DRep key hash under any staking part, so its value counts as leaving (#358 class).
With the account's collateral in it, a collateral return that isn't the account's own address is refused.
A collateral return on the other network (Byron by its magic) is refused.
at_risk = the account's collateral less what returns to the account: its exact loss if scripts fail, even when the site's collateral is mixed in.
guards.test: cip30_test.rs collateral_at_the_stake_keys_own_address_is_the_accounts (partly); none pins the mixed case

guards.stops: A transaction marked to fail (is_valid false) with the account's collateral is refused.
guards.test: cip30_test.rs (failing_tx_hex, line 1063: err contains "marked to fail")

guards.stops: An output on the other network (Byron by its network magic) is refused.

own_address: an output is the account's only with an in-range payment key AND the account's stake key; anything else is paid (#359 class); own_payment_key flags the account's key under another staking part.
A pool registration naming the account's stake key an owner is refused (its stake would pledge for the pool).
An old-style deregistration of the account's key without a known deposit is refused; with one, the refund is counted in what the account puts in.
A withdrawal from a reward address on the other network is refused; the account's own withdrawal counts in staking.
A proposal whose deposit returns on the other network is refused.
A payment key's or the DRep key's signature over any input or collateral the wallet can't find is refused, whatever partialSign says.
Any signature over a transaction nothing ties to the wallet's network (no output, withdrawal, network id or found input) is refused, so the stake key can't act on the other network.
The net counts what the account puts in from staking (withdrawals, its deposit and DRep refunds) beside its UTxOs, so rewards paid to others show as leaving.
Checked sums of ADA and token amounts from rows and outputs: an overflow is refused in words, never wrapped (seedelf-wasm has no overflow checks).
guards.test: none found for the overflow branch

guards.stops: read_value stops at 1,000 policies plus tokens, so a site's amount can't exhaust the module's memory.
raw_map/raw_vkeys don't size by a count the bytes chose, so a huge header can't abort WebAssembly.
Without partialSign, a transaction that needs anyone else's signature (or has unknown inputs) is not signed.
The view refuses a transaction with bytes after its end, so the hex shown is the transaction itself.

checked_ok: build::tx_id (seedelf-core/src/build.rs:1201) hashes the body's bytes exactly as sent, so the witness signs what the ledger hashes; inspect reads the same bytes it signs.

No preallocation from a CBOR count anywhere in pallas-codec/primitives/addresses 0.35.1 or minicbor 0.25.1 (grep for with_capacity/reserve: none); cip30's raw_map/raw_vkeys and decode's map_fields/redeemers/script_list consume bytes per entry. A 9-byte header claiming 2^64 items can't abort WebAssembly.

nests_within counts every array, map and tag, and the bytes any tag wraps. That matches pallas-codec CborWrap, which takes any tag number and only a definite byte string (utils.rs:528-538). It ends only on genuine malformations, at the same point minicbor would, and never under-counts what Pallas recurses into. Byron address payloads, decoded from an output's plain bytes, are fixed-depth (byron.rs AddrAttrProperty).

No reachable panic in either file: decimal's casts are bounded (now ≤ 2559), cbor_head shifts at most 8 bytes, Items(Some(0)) is popped before any decrement, and limits/ends are checked before slicing.
Arithmetic on outside values is checked (Amount::add/add_token, add_staking) or kept to i128/saturating for figures only; counts use plain + and can't overflow.

Inputs: own by payment key (in range), stake key or DRep key (governance) under any staking part (#358 class); a script's input goes to contract_held, never the net; a found input of another's key goes to foreign_keys.

Outputs: own only with an in-range payment key AND the account's stake key (#359 class); the collateral return uses the same rule; the account's key under any other staking part is flagged ownPaymentKey and counted as paid.

Net = own outputs − (own inputs + withdrawals + own deposit/DRep refunds). The fee, deposits, donation and proposal deposits all leave through it. Reference inputs and collateral are rightly kept out.
at_risk = the account's collateral − the return to the account: exact even when the site's collateral is mixed in, and the ledger forbids tokens left in collateral.
Network: network_id, every output (Byron by magic), collateral return, rows, withdrawals and proposals are checked; a transaction with nothing naming the network gets no signature.

Duplicates and unknown fields: Pallas's derived body map is last-wins and skips unknown keys (minicbor-derive 0.15.3 decode.rs:359-376), and Pallas keeps duplicate multiasset entries, which of_value sums. To my reading of cardano-ledger-binary, Conway refuses a repeated body key, unknown body keys, and duplicate map keys and set elements from protocol 9, so none of these readings reaches the chain (see notes).

Validity window: valid_from/valid_until reach the UI as JSON numbers, and slotText (format.ts:131) answers undefined past Date's range, so the window says "Never" for a huge ttl; it can't read as an early expiry.

The CIP-20 note in the sign window is raw text, but it sits in a `unicode-bidi: isolate` <pre> labelled as the site's note (styles.css:3703, DappApprovals.tsx:1279), so a bidi override can't leak past it.
signData: a DRep ID or the DRep key's enterprise address only with governance; the network is checked for addresses; the COSE_Sign1 and COSE_Key follow CIP-8; the payload is unhashed, as said.
attach_witnesses copies the body and the other witness entries byte for byte, so the transaction id and the script data hash hold; sessions.ts:4479 checks the id again after attaching.

Rows reaching WebAssembly are trimmed (koios.ts:67-83: the datum JSON is nulled and the reference script reduced to hash/size/type/bytes), so serde_json's 128-level limit can't be tripped by a stranger's deep datum JSON.

decode.rs: every number the bytes decide is a decimal string; constructor tags map to 0–127, tag 102 included; big numbers are exact; text from the chain is escaped; a register is read only at the Seedelf contract by script hash on the network asked; the metadata hash is compared against the aux bytes as written; trailing bytes are refused.
notes: Duplicate map keys, for a verifier with ledger source. The extension's TS `bodyField` (cbor.ts:118-130, which feeds resolve, keptApart, heldForLovejoin and stakeDeposit) takes a body key's FIRST occurrence. Pallas takes the LAST, and cip30's of_value SUMS duplicate multiasset entries. I believe Conway's ledger refuses all three shapes (the sparse record decoder rejects a repeated key; decodeMap/decodeSet reject duplicates from protocol 9). If so, nothing reaches the chain and the worst case is the collateral-as-input check being bypassed in a transaction that can't land. If the ledger instead took one duplicate multiasset entry, an own output written {A:100, A:1} would read as 101 back to the user while the ledger kept 1: a critical understatement. Please confirm against cardano-ledger-binary's Coders/Decoder before closing it; I couldn't fetch it offline.

The 128-level nesting guard is pinned only by native tests (2 MB+ thread stacks). No WebAssembly test decodes a transaction near the boundary: inspect, then decode_tx's plutus_tree and serde_json, in the 1 MiB wasm stack. A wasm/tests/*.mjs case with a datum about 120 levels deep, through both, would hold the margin. I found no evidence of an overflow.

attach_witnesses (cip30.rs:2103-2108) keeps a witness already present for the same vkey and drops the wallet's own. If Minswap's built swap carried a bad witness for the session key, the swap would fail at submit with no money lost. Replacing the vkey's entry with the wallet's own would be strictly better. It is the aggregator's own denial of service, so I didn't make it a finding.

The register is read two ways. cip30 reads Pallas's re-encoded inline datum (output_parts:982), decode.rs the bytes as written. So a register whose 48-byte points are written as chunked (indefinite) byte strings shows as "register" in the sign window, which is right since the contract sees the same bytes, but as no register in Transaction details. The view errs on the cautious side, but the two disagree.

OwnOutput.inline_datum is Pallas's re-encoding, not the bytes as written. It is kept for chaining and handed back through getUtxos, equal in content but not necessarily in bytes for non-canonical encodings. It's harmless for key-locked outputs.

decode.rs auxiliary(): a ShelleyMa-form metadata script's hash comes from Pallas's re-encoding (encode_fragment), not the bytes as written. The PostAlonzo form reads raw bytes. This affects the display only.

architecture.md ("It refuses the other network, a collateral return to someone else, and a transaction marked to fail its scripts") and wasm/README.md:92 leave out the code's condition. Both refusals apply only when the account's own collateral is in the transaction (cip30.rs:1312, 1330). This is a docs nit for the docs lane.

signData (cip30.rs:2269-2271) signs for any Shelley address under an in-range payment key, whatever its staking part: base with a stranger's stake key, pointer or enterprise. The transaction side calls such an output someone else's (#359's rule). I found no concrete harm, since the signature proves control of a key the user does hold. I note it for consistency.

Cross-lane, for the contract-scan, sessions and data-layer lanes: matching the Seedelf contract by Koios `payment_cred` alone (contract-scan.ts:429, sessions.ts:2954) can't tell a key credential from a script credential. A key address whose key hash is the contract's (w2#2's shape) carrying the user's register would be unspendable. Check whether such a row can enter the private balance.

Older swap sessions with the shared stake part are inspected with stakeIndex 0 (sessions.ts:4386). The shared part is dapp_address(Receive i), not the one-time root's 2/0, so if any such session still exists, its own change and collateral return would read as someone else's. All site sessions are created with ownStake: true, so readTx's `stakeIndex: holder.index` is right. Out of lane; a pointer only.

w2#4 also has a non-adversarial form: a user who deploys a reference script to their own address through some dApp gets a large UTxO (min-ADA for the script). getUtxos lists it first (largestFirst), so the next sites' transactions fail at submit until it's locked.
